arabicExcerpts.text: بَلَىٰ قَٰدِرِينَ عَلَىٰٓ أَن نُّسَوِّيَ بَنَانَهُۥ
يُنَبَّؤُاْ ٱلۡإِنسَٰنُ يَوۡمَئِذِۭ بِمَا قَدَّمَ وَأَخَّرَ

mainSubject.label: Oaths by the Day of Resurrection and the reproaching soul affirming bone-reassembly and fingertip-proportioning power; man's desire to persist in sin producing the question when is the Day; when vision is dazzled, the moon darkens and sun and moon are joined, man asks where escape is — there is none, permanence belongs only to the Lord that Day; man informed of what he sent ahead and kept back, becoming a witness against himself even if he offers excuses

subordinateSubjects.label: Oath sworn by the Day of Resurrection
And by the reproaching soul as further confirmation
Does man think We will not assemble his bones
Yes — We are able even to proportion his fingertips
But man desires to continue in sin
He asks when the Day of Resurrection is
And the sun and moon are joined
Man will ask on that Day where escape is
To your Lord alone is permanence that Day
Man informed of what he sent ahead and kept back
Rather man against himself will be a witness
Even if he presents his excuses

humanConditionsAndSpiritualStates.label: Desire to persist in sin producing denial of resurrection timing
Cosmic dissolution — dazzled vision, darkened moon, joined sun and moon — prompting the futile escape question
Self-witness against oneself despite offered excuses

relationships.label: Bone reassembly and fingertip proportioning demonstrating resurrection power
No refuge exists; permanence belongs solely to the Lord on that Day
Deeds sent ahead and kept back disclosed to man on that Day

notes: Wave 11 genuine re-extraction. Boundaries follow the text: P1 closes with the self-witness and excuses statement (15) before the Quran-recitation instruction opens (16); P2 ends with the contorted-faces-backbreaking-expectation scene (25) before the deathbed sequence begins (26); P3 runs through collar-bones, separation certainty, leg-wound, procession and the swaggering-denier woe (26-35); P4 covers the neglected-question, embryological stages and the closing resurrection-ability argument (36-40).
